data.content:
Zeus
Zeus was the god of the sky, ruler of the gods, and father of Hermes, Athena, and Ares. Zeus punished inhospitality and rewarded Baucis and Philemon's kindness.<SEP>Brother of Hades and Poseidon who assigned Hestia responsibility for the gods' necessities and made Hestia goddess of the home and family.

Hermes
Hermes was Zeus's mischievous son, inventor of the lyre, and a messenger between gods and mortals. Hermes stole Apollo's cattle and exchanged the lyre for permission to keep the cattle.

Baucis
Baucis was a poor, elderly woman married to Philemon. Baucis welcomed Zeus and Hermes and later lived as a priestess.

Philemon
Philemon was Baucis's poor, elderly husband. Philemon welcomed Zeus and Hermes and later lived as a priest.

Baucis and Philemon's Hut
Baucis and Philemon's hut sheltered Zeus and Hermes, survived a destructive flood, and was transformed into a temple.

Temple
The temple was transformed from Baucis and Philemon's hut by Zeus and became the couple's lifelong home as priestess and priest.

Wine Jug
The wine jug was Baucis and Philemon's only jug of wine, offered to Zeus and Hermes and later discovered refilled.

Zeus's Flood
Zeus's flood punished people who refused food and shelter to Zeus and Hermes, destroying every home in the valley except Baucis and Philemon's hut.

Oak and Linden Trees
The oak and linden trees were the forms Baucis and Philemon assumed after death, with entwined branches.

Athena
Athena was Zeus's strong and wise daughter, born wearing armour and carrying a shield and sword. Athena gave an olive tree to Athens and became the city's protector.<SEP>Goddess who offered to make Paris a courageous and successful soldier in exchange for favorable judgment.

Poseidon
Poseidon was the god of the seas and Athena's rival. Poseidon drove a golden chariot, carried a trident, and offered a saltwater river to the city later named Athens.<SEP>Brother of Hades and Zeus who wished to marry Hestia.

Athens
Athens was the city whose citizens chose Athena as protector and named the city after Athena. Athens became strong and prosperous and is the capital of Greece.

Greece
Greece is the country whose capital city is Athens.

Poseidon's Trident
Poseidon's trident was used to strike the ground and release water that became a river.

Poseidon's River
Poseidon's river was a saltwater river offered to the citizens of the city later named Athens. The river flowed to the sea.

Olive Tree
The olive tree was Athena's gift to the citizens of Athens, providing wood, edible olives, and olives from which cooking oil could be obtained.

Olive Wood
Olive wood from Athena's gift could be used for building and heating.

Olives
Olives growing on Athena's olive tree could be eaten and provided oil for cooking.

Olive Oil
Olive oil obtained from the olives could be used for cooking.

Poseidon's Flood
Poseidon's flood was caused by Poseidon after the citizens chose Athena as the city's protector.

Apollo
Apollo was a god whose cattle were stolen by Hermes. Enchanted by Hermes's music, Apollo accepted the lyre in exchange for the cattle and subsequently carried the instrument.<SEP>Artemis's twin brother who wished to marry Hestia.

Lyre
The lyre was the first musical instrument, created by Hermes by tying strings across a tortoise shell. Hermes later gave the lyre to Apollo.

Apollo's Cattle
Apollo's cattle were a herd stolen and hidden by Hermes. Apollo later allowed Hermes to keep the cattle in exchange for the lyre.

Winged Hat and Sandals
Hermes's winged hat and sandals enabled quick travel and helped Hermes deliver messages between gods and mortals.

Ares
Ares was the god of war and Zeus's son. Ares supported the Trojans after promising to help the Greeks and was wounded by Diomedes.

Trojan War
The Trojan War was the conflict during which Ares promised to help the Greeks but instead supported the Trojans at Aphrodite's urging.<SEP>Ten-year war that followed Helen and Paris's flight to Troy and the king of Sparta's declaration of war.

Greeks
The Greeks were the side Ares initially promised to support during the Trojan War.

Trojans
The Trojans were the side Ares supported during the Trojan War after persuasion by Aphrodite.

Aphrodite
Aphrodite was the beautiful goddess of love. Aphrodite persuaded Ares to support the Trojans and once unintentionally started a war.<SEP>Beautiful goddess of love who won Paris's judgment, unintentionally helped cause the Trojan War, and became Hephaestus's wife.

Diomedes
Diomedes was a Greek mortal challenged by Ares who inflicted a minor wound on Ares.

Eris
Eris was a goddess who enjoyed causing trouble and made a golden apple bearing the words “For the fairest.”<SEP>Goddess who enjoyed causing trouble and created a golden apple to provoke competition among Hera, Aphrodite, and Athena.

Golden Apple
The golden apple was made by Eris, inscribed “For the fairest,” and left where Hera, Aphrodite, and Athena would find the apple.<SEP>Apple created by Eris, inscribed with the words “For the fairest,” and left for Hera, Aphrodite, and Athena.

Hera
Hera was one of the goddesses Eris intended to find the golden apple.<SEP>Goddess who offered Paris power and was trapped by a golden throne created by her son Hephaestus.

Hermes's Mother
Hermes's mother became sleepy while listening to Hermes play the lyre. Hermes left to explore while Hermes's mother slept and later returned to Hermes's mother's arms.

Hermes's Birth Cave
Hermes's birth cave was the birthplace of Hermes and the place Hermes returned to after hiding Apollo's stolen cattle.

Tortoise Shell
The tortoise shell was found by Hermes and used as the body of the first lyre.

Lyre Strings
The lyre strings were tied across a tortoise shell by Hermes and plucked to make the first music.

Poseidon's Golden Chariot
Poseidon's golden chariot was the vehicle driven by Poseidon.

Athena's Spear
Athena's spear was used by Athena to strike the ground, causing an olive tree to grow as a gift for the city's citizens.

Paris
Mortal chosen to judge the fairest goddess who selected Aphrodite and later ran away with Helen to Troy.

Helen
Woman described as the most beautiful in the world, married to the king of Sparta before running away with Paris.

King of Sparta
Helen's husband who sent soldiers to declare war on Troy after Helen ran away with Paris.

Hades
Brother of Zeus and Poseidon who ruled the Underworld, kept the dead there, and conditionally permitted Orpheus to retrieve Orpheus's wife.

Orpheus
Wonderful singer who entered the Underworld to recover a deceased wife but violated Hades's condition by looking back during departure.

Orpheus's Wife
Deceased wife of Orpheus who had to remain in the Underworld forever after Orpheus looked back during departure.

Hephaestus
Hera's son who created a trapping golden throne for revenge, later freed Hera, and received Aphrodite as a wife.

Dionysus
God of wine described as Zeus's half-son who was asked to intoxicate Hephaestus and later received Hestia's throne.

Artemis
Apollo's twin sister and goddess of hunting and the moon who was a skilled fighter and evaded Alpheus by covering her face in mud.

Alpheus
River god who fell in love with Artemis and unsuccessfully pursued Artemis through a forest.

Artemis's Nymphs
Female followers of Artemis who covered their faces in mud, preventing Alpheus from distinguishing Artemis from the followers.

Hestia
Oldest god of Olympus who refused marriage, became goddess of the home and family, supplied the gods' necessities, and surrendered a throne to Dionysus.

Demeter
Demeter appeared to Erysichthon in goddess form, sent away the slaves, and cursed Erysichthon with insatiable hunger.<SEP>Goddess of agriculture who punished Erysichthon with insatiable hunger for cutting down a dedicated oak tree.

Erysichthon
Erysichthon continued an unspecified activity regardless and was punished by Demeter with a curse of hunger that could never be satisfied.<SEP>Arrogant, selfish, and greedy man who cut down Demeter's oak tree to make a banqueting table and received a curse of insatiable hunger.

Sparta
Kingdom ruled by Helen's husband.

Troy
Destination of Helen and Paris's flight and target of the war declared by the king of Sparta.

Underworld
World of the dead ruled by Hades, where Orpheus attempted to retrieve a deceased wife.

Mount Olympus
Place of the gods where Hephaestus freed Hera, Hestia received responsibilities, and Dionysus demanded a throne.

Thessaly
Region containing the huge oak tree dedicated to Demeter.

Hades's Chariot
Chariot belonging to Hades and drawn by four black horses.

Four Black Horses
Four horses that drew Hades's chariot.

Golden Throne
Throne created by Hephaestus as a revenge gift that trapped Hera with unbreakable chains.

Unbreakable Chains
Chains that bound Hera after Hera sat on Hephaestus's golden throne.

Key to Olympus
Key given by Zeus to Hestia as a token of appreciation after Hestia refused marriage.

Demeter's Oak Tree
Huge oak in Thessaly dedicated to Demeter, decorated by local people, used for vows, and cut down by Erysichthon.

Curse of Insatiable Hunger
The curse imposed by Demeter ensured that Erysichthon's hunger would never be satisfied.<SEP>Punishment imposed by Demeter that prevented Erysichthon's hunger from ever being satisfied.

Erysichthon's Slaves
Group ordered to cut down Demeter's oak tree who refused the task and were later sent away by Demeter.

Love
Domain associated with Aphrodite, who was identified as the goddess of love.

Hunting
Activity associated with Artemis, who hunted in forests and was identified as the goddess of hunting.

Moon
Celestial object associated with Artemis's role as a goddess.

Wine
Substance associated with Dionysus, who was identified as the god of wine.

Agriculture
Domain associated with Demeter, who was identified as the goddess of agriculture.

Home and Family
Domain assigned to Hestia by Zeus when Zeus made Hestia the goddess of the home and family.

Bow and Arrow
Hunting equipment used by Artemis in the forests.

Banqueting Table
Intended product for which Erysichthon ordered the cutting of Demeter's oak tree.

Hestia's Throne
Throne that Hestia willingly surrendered to Dionysus after Dionysus arrived at Olympus demanding a throne.

Slaves
The slaves were a group sent away by Demeter before Demeter punished Erysichthon.
